title.narrative: Interpeace: att mäta utveckling i postkonflikt

description.narrative: Interpeace kommer att utveckla en metod och verktyg för att identifiera och bedöma källor till motståndskraft (resiliens) mot våld och väpnad konflikt. Metoden kommer att baseras och utprövas med hjälp av tre fallstudier: Guatemala, Östtimor och Liberia.

Interpeace will develop a method and tools for identify, assess and address sources of resilience to violence and armed conflict. The the method will be based on experiences from and piloted in three countries: Guatemala, East Timor and Liberia.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative: General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2016Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: Sida assesses that Interpeace has successfully, throughout the “Framework for Assessing Resilience” (FAR) programme, developed tools and a framework for monitoring and assessing resilience within societies. Most encompassing is the "Guidance Note" - including a conceptual and strategic framework as well as guidance and reflections of the process. The Guidance Note is an analytical tool, including 6 categories of indicators designed to be context specific, as well as an action-oriented approach including strategies of programming and policy action. These tools and methods were developed in relation to three pilot countries, Liberia, Timor-Leste and Guatemala. In all three pilot countries local stakeholders participated in the development of specific country notes that served as a base for testing more generic applications of the framework included in the Guidance Note and are a critical component of the overall framework. In total 8,580 Timorese, Liberians and Guatemalans were involved in the project. The process of developing this framework included cross-country learning between the three pilot countries, specifically through workshops. Interpeace concludes that they have successfully managed to attract interest in resilience internationally and will continue their work in collaboration with international actors.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
